title: Delivery Fleet Optimization
short_description: Learn how a delivery company models vehicles, depots and delivery locations as a graph to organize routes and assignments efficiently while reducing distance and travel time.

real_world_context.problem: A delivery company has multiple vehicles and delivery locations and needs to organize routes and assignments efficiently while reducing distance and travel time. The road network is modeled as a graph where depots and delivery points are nodes and roads are edges. The company must explore reachable locations, confirm routes, find the fastest paths, assign deliveries to vehicles greedily, and decide how many deliveries can fit within a time budget.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Efficiently routing and assigning a fleet reduces distance and travel time, which lowers fuel cost and improves delivery speed. The right graph and optimization algorithms decide how well the fleet serves all delivery locations.

learning_objectives: Understand how a delivery region and road network can be represented as a graph.
Use Graph BFS to explore delivery locations reachable from a depot.
Use Graph DFS to detect whether a vehicle can reach a delivery location.
Use Dijkstra's Algorithm to find the fastest route between a depot and a delivery point.
Use A* Pathfinding to guide a vehicle toward its delivery destination.
Use a Greedy approach to assign deliveries to vehicles efficiently.
Use Binary Search on Answer to find how many deliveries fit within a time budget.
completion_message: You have completed the Delivery Fleet Optimization mission. You have learned how graph traversal, weighted shortest-path, guided search, greedy assignment and binary-search-on-answer techniques help a delivery company organize routes and assignments efficiently.
